decision.why: Data inspection established a seven-song pilot and available baseline artifacts. Measured baseline failures are needed to choose the smallest useful experiment before spending the four-worker budget.
decision.hypothesis: Melody, chord recognition, or transposition errors are concentrated enough that a targeted experiment can distinguish a useful improvement.
decision.expected_observation: Baseline melody and chord error counts, timing and transposition failures, and sample-level differences that identify a concrete intervention.

limits: References are supplied labels, not a musician-audited gold set.
Seven song groups, short excerpts, all with empty key signatures; no held-out generalization claim.
Primary metric is sequence edit error on pitch plus rational duration, with matching ties merged. Includes rests.
Chord score measures ordered root, kind, bass and explicit extensions; chord timing is not scored.
No full notation, voice alignment, repeat-playback, lyric or accidental-display fidelity metric.
Missing or unparseable outputs count as all reference events deleted; their unparsed insertions cannot be counted.
An edit error rate can exceed 100 percent; it is not accuracy.
No correction-time study or calibrated confidence thresholds yet.
Latency includes per-image Audiveris startup, excludes neural load time; some runs overlapped, so do not compare speed as controlled performance.
Transcoda canonical header/terminator restoration changes no pitches or durations. Raw outputs are retained.
No weights trained, no labels sent to inference, no paid API calls.

decision.argument: Which curated sources support feasible image-derived chord recognition and editable **kern export with transposition, including limitations of chord timing and low-resolution melody recognition? Prioritize methods using Pillow, Tesseract, music21 or Verovio without installing Audiveris.
decision.why: Enlarging inputs leaves 87 melody errors and 30 missing chords on the seven-sample pilot. Source guidance can identify a small, feasible experiment that isolates chord recovery without conflating it with melody changes.
decision.hypothesis: A separate chord-recognition pass can recover omitted chord symbols while preserving the measured enlarged-baseline melody.
decision.expected_observation: Sources describe chord-region extraction, symbol normalization and notation export constraints, with explicit limitations on onset alignment and transposition validation.

decision.why: The paired enlarged baseline misses 30 of 38 chords while its eight predicted chords match. The source audit identifies absent text-to-harmony integration as a concrete failure. A chord-only intervention isolates this hypothesis and preserves the strongest measured baseline melody within the four-experiment budget.
decision.hypothesis: Image-derived chord OCR and structured parsing can reduce chord deletions without increasing melody error; ambiguous symbols and onset alignment may remain unresolved.
decision.expected_observation: More than eight matched chords and lower chord error than 0.78947, with unchanged parseable baseline melody. Spurious OCR chords or unsupported normalization would falsify the proposed benefit. Timing artifacts and round-trip checks will not establish audited timing or musician approval.

config.success_criteria: Deliver sealed predictions for all seven pilot images, parse-validation results, and a per-image chord provenance table with crop coordinates, raw OCR, normalized symbols and timing uncertainty. Verify melody event sequences remain identical to the supplied baseline wherever parseable; report any baseline parse failure separately without inventing melody. Protected evaluation must compare chord error and melody error with enlarged Audiveris on the same seven images. Include a transposition round-trip check for melody and chord root/bass, identified as structural validation rather than measured musical accuracy.
